chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: Floor shows, Small's Paradise and Stormy Weather
summary: Patsy says the club dance shows dried up as combos came in; she worked Small's, Elks Rendezvous, Tiny Bradshaw and Stormy Weather.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But all this time you were coming up, there was always dancing.

Yes, yes. They had shows, yes, like Small's in New York was well known for shows but see after the era, when they started having these combos of singing, they had their own choreographers, so they make a show in itself,
and then they ask such fantastic prices so then they cut out the shows, you know, with girls.
The dancing was almost an extension of music.

I said, I worked with Tiny Bradshaw there, because I was commuting back and forth from New York to Chicago to do the shows. In fact, I was doing two shows at one time, Small's and Elk's Rendevous and the place in Chicago.
It was in New York. And of course, working with Lena Horne in Stormy Weather and Bill Robinson and Fats Waller. They were all in Stormy Weather, the picture.
